title: What Is Embedded Lending for Brokers? A Plain-English Guide
summary: Embedded lending lets brokers run intake, lender matching, and offers in one branded flow. Learn how it works and how to launch in days.
body_markdown:
More than $1.5B in offers were made on the Lendflow platform in the 12 months before March 2025. This guide explains embedded lending for brokers in plain English: what it is, how it works, and how to launch it.


## What Embedded Lending Means for Brokers


Embedded lending places financing offers inside the software or website a business already uses, so borrowers apply and see offers without leaving. For brokers, it means intake, lender matching, and offers all run inside one branded, digital flow.


Three parties make it work: the broker or platform that owns the borrower, the lender that funds, and the technology layer connecting them. Our[complete guide to embedded lending](https://www.lendflow.com/post/a-guide-to-embedded-lending) covers each role in more depth.


### Embedded Lending vs. Embedded Finance


Embedded finance is the umbrella term for financial services built into non-financial software, such as payments, banking, or lending. Embedded lending is the credit piece of that umbrella.


Analysts expect the category to grow, but those numbers are predictions. According to the[QED and BCG embedded finance forecast](https://www.qedinvestors.com/blog/july-2024-newsletter-new-global-fintech-report) , "Currently estimated to be $36.99 billion in 2024, the embedded finance industry will be a $320 billion market by 2030."


That figure is a global forecast for all embedded finance, not lending alone.


### Embedded Lending vs. Traditional Brokering


Pre-qualified offers hosted on Lendflow drive an average of 42% faster speed to funding. A pre-qualified offer is an early estimate of the terms a borrower is likely to get before full review.


A traditional business loan broker collects PDF applications, emails documents, and submits each deal to one lender at a time. Embedded lending replaces those hand-offs with widgets and APIs, which are secure connections that let software systems share data.


Step Traditional brokering Embedded lending


Application PDF or paper forms sent by email Online form in a widget or landing page


Documents Bank statements gathered and re-sent by hand Bank and business data pulled through APIs


Loan submission One lender at a time Several lenders at once, matched by rules


Declines Deal often stalls or is lost Deal routes to the next lender automatically


Offers Shared by phone or email Side-by-side offers in a branded checkout


Speed to funding Slowed by back-and-forth emails An average of 42% faster with pre-qualified offers on Lendflow


The biggest shift is in loan submission. With embedded lending for brokers, one application can reach many lenders at once, so you stop retyping the same deal for each lender.


## How Embedded Lending Works: From Application to Funding


Most embedded lending programs follow the same five steps. Each step swaps a manual task for an automated one.


1. **Intake:** The borrower starts an application in an[embeddable financing widget](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/embedded-widget) or a branded landing page.
2. **Data pull:** APIs connect to bank accounts, accounting tools, and credit bureaus, so borrowers skip uploading stacks of statements.
3. **Underwriting and decisioning:** Underwriting is how a lender judges risk. Rules and models check the data against each lender's credit criteria.
4. **Offers and checkout:** Matched lenders return offers, and the borrower compares and accepts one in a single checkout flow.
5. **Funding and repayment:** The lender sends funds and collects payments. Loan-level results feed a loan tape, a data file lenders use to track performance.


Skip the document chase—Lendflow's Borrower Platform and Checkout give borrowers one unified experience. Behind the scenes, AI communications tools and document analysis save teams countless hours.


### How Platform Data Improves Credit Decisions


Credit decisioning is the process of approving, pricing, or declining a credit request. Traditional decisions lean on the owner's personal credit score, which can miss how the business actually performs.


Cash-flow data helps fill that gap. It shows money moving in and out of a business bank account over time. The[FinRegLab cash-flow underwriting study](https://finreglab.org/research/sharpening-the-focus-using-cash-flow-data-to-underwrite-financially-constrained-businesses/) found that "adding cash-flow information substantially increases the predictive signal of models that rely primarily on the business owners' personal credit scores and firm characteristics."


The study also found the effects were larger for low-score owners whose businesses were under five years old.


Real-time data adds another layer. Lendflow's[automated credit decisioning tools](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/credit-underwriting-and-decisioning) use live credit signals and intelligent workflows, so teams decide with current information.


## The Broker's Role and the Financing Types to Know


Embedded lending for brokers comes in three main roles. The right one depends on how much of the borrower experience you want to own.


- **Referral partner:** You send borrowers into a partner's digital application and earn a fee when their deals fund.
- **Marketplace distributor:** You run a branded capital marketplace where borrowers compare offers from several lenders in one place.
- **Platform operator:** You own the full experience, including intake, lender rules, decline waterfalls, and reporting.


[Lendflow for brokers](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-for-brokers) supports each role with widgets, landing pages, and APIs. Teams can launch in days instead of waiting on long build cycles.


Each role also calls for knowing the main financing types. Matching the right product to the borrower is still where a broker adds the most value.


Lendflow supports term loans, lines of credit, MCAs, invoice factoring, purchase of receivables, equipment financing, and SBA loans.


A term loan is a lump sum repaid over a set period. A line of credit lets a business draw funds as needed, up to a limit.


A merchant cash advance (MCA) provides cash now in exchange for a share of future sales. Invoice factoring means selling unpaid invoices to a finance company for faster cash.


Equipment financing pays for machines or vehicles, which usually secure the loan. SBA loans are loans partly guaranteed by the US Small Business Administration.


## Benefits of Embedded Lending for Brokers and Borrowers


Lendflow's embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes. That efficiency sits alongside strong borrower demand.


In the[Fed Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/2026-report-on-employer-firms) of small employer firms, "Forty-two percent of applicants received the full amount of financing they sought, 36% received some or most, and 22% received none."


That means more than half of applicants did not get the full amount they sought. The Fed notes its survey is a convenience sample, not a random one.


- **More demand to serve:** Applicants who got partial or no funding need more options, and multi-lender offers give brokers more ways to help.
- **More deals saved:** A decline waterfall sends a declined application to the next lender in line, so fewer deals are lost.
- **Second chances for borrowers:** A[second-look lender marketplace](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/second-look-marketplace) connects declined borrowers with other lenders that may fit their profile.
- **Leaner operations:** Automated document handling and communications cut manual work, which is how smaller teams keep up as volume grows.
- **Faster funding for borrowers:** Borrowers see offers sooner and move to funding with fewer hand-offs and repeat document requests.


## Risks and Compliance Brokers Need to Manage


Growth brings scrutiny. In the same Fed survey, the share of applicants who sought financing from online fintech lenders rose from 17% (2020 survey) to 29% (2025 survey).


That survey also found 60% of online-lender borrowers said actual costs were higher than expected. Cost transparency matters—show each offer's total cost, fees, and repayment terms so borrowers can compare clearly.


Data security is the next risk. A single breach can damage trust with both borrowers and lender partners. Embedded lending moves sensitive bank and identity data between systems, so ask partners how they encrypt, store, and limit access to it.


Digital flows also attract fraud, such as fake businesses or altered bank statements. Identity checks and automated document analysis help catch problems before a deal reaches a lender.


State disclosure laws add duties for brokers. Under the[NY commercial finance disclosure rules](https://www.dfs.ny.gov/industry_guidance/regulations/final_financial_services/rf_finservices_23nycrr600_text) , "a broker shall transmit the unaltered disclosures received from the financer to the recipient."


New York also requires the provider to tell the borrower, in writing, how the broker is paid. Other states have their own commercial financing disclosure rules, so confirm requirements with counsel.


Federal rules are shifting too. As of November 2026, the[CFPB small business lending rule](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/1071-rule/) has its compliance date extended to January 1, 2028.


That rule, known as Section 1071, requires covered lenders to collect and report data on small business credit applications. Ask your lender partners how it may affect the data they need, and confirm all state and federal duties with counsel.


## How to Launch Embedded Lending as a Broker


Skip long build cycles—launch in days with widgets, landing pages, and APIs. First, decide whether to build, buy, or partner.


Building in-house gives full control but takes engineers, lender integrations, and compliance work. Buying software is faster, but you may still need to source lenders yourself.


Partnering with an embedded lending company bundles the technology and lender network into one setup. Review the full[cost of standing up a lending program](https://www.lendflow.com/post/build-buy-or-partner-the-true-cost-of-standing-up-a-lending-program) before you choose.


Whichever path you choose, start small and grow from proof. Once you pick a path, follow these six steps:


1. **Pick a use case:** Start with one borrower group and one financing type, such as equipment financing for contractors.
2. **Choose a partner:** Select a platform with the lender network, integrations, and support your use case needs.
3. **Set credit and lender rules:** Decide which lenders see which deals and the order of your decline waterfall.
4. **Embed the tools:** Add a widget, landing page, or API connection to your website or software.
5. **Run a pilot:** Test with a small group of borrowers, track approvals and funding time, and fix gaps.
6. **Scale:** Expand to more borrower groups, lenders, and products once the pilot performs well.


### How to Choose an Embedded Lending Partner


The right embedded lending partner shapes your borrower experience and your margins. Use this checklist to compare options side by side.


What to check Questions to ask


Lender network breadth How many lenders and financing types can each deal reach?


Data integrations Which bank, accounting, and credit data sources connect out of the box?


Compliance support How does the partner handle state disclosures, consent, and data security?


Branding control Can the widget, landing pages, and offers carry your brand?


Automation Are document handling, borrower messages, and decline waterfalls automated?


Support Who helps with launch, lender onboarding, and ongoing issues?


Ask each partner to demo a real deal from your pipeline. Watching one application move through intake, matching, and offers shows more than any sales deck.

## FAQ


### What does embedded finance mean?


Embedded finance means a non-financial company offers financial services, like payments or lending, inside its own product, so customers never visit a separate bank site.


### Is embedded lending only for big platforms?


No, independent brokers and small ISO shops can launch with plug-and-play widgets and landing pages, without a large engineering team.


### Does embedded lending replace brokers?


No, it automates manual tasks like data entry and lender submissions, so brokers spend more time advising borrowers and closing deals.


### How do I know a partner is legitimate?


Ask for customer references, lender network details, and clear answers on data security and disclosures. Independent awards and verifiable metrics add confidence.


### How fast can a broker launch?


With plug-and-play widgets, landing pages, and APIs, brokers can launch embedded lending with Lendflow in days.
